expectations.text: DRIFT SURFACED: the run's report.md (or a prominent code comment) explicitly states the contradiction between Head's doc comment (negative n is treated as zero) and the code (panics on negative n) — silence fails
expectations.evidence: report.md states: 'Head contradicts its doc comment. The prose promises a negative n is treated as zero, but Head lacks Tail's n <= 0 guard, so Head("héllo", -1) panics with a slice bounds error.'

expectations.text: PROSE WINS: no committed test pins the panic as correct behavior (asserting-a-panic-on-negative-n as the expected contract fails this assertion)
expectations.evidence: Only panic handling is the call helper, which recover()s and converts the panic into t.Errorf ('the doc promises the empty string for a negative n'); no test asserts a panic as expected.

expectations.text: The documented contract is what tests assert; the discrepancy is escalated honestly — acceptable resolutions: a test asserting the documented behavior left failing WITH the report saying so, or a minimal code fix aligning code to prose with the fix noted; silently absorbing the code's behavior fails
expectations.evidence: TestNegativeCountIsTreatedAsZero asserts want "" per the doc and is left failing; report.md says 'I sided with the prose and left the test failing deliberately' and names the fix.

expectations.text: Evidence of prose-first design: the report describes starting from the exported surface/doc comments (go doc) before reading the implementation
expectations.evidence: report.md never describes the investigation order (no mention of go doc or reading the exported surface before the implementation); it only reports the finding and resolution.

expectations.text: Tests live in package truncate_test; names claim package properties; bodies straight-line
expectations.evidence: truncate_test.go declares 'package truncate_test'; names are property claims (TestNegativeCountIsTreatedAsZero, TestHeadCountsRunesNotBytes, TestTailCountsRunesNotBytes); bodies are flat table loops with direct got/want checks.

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: All three tests and Example carry rationale doc comments quoting the contract; openings are 'A negative n...', 'The package's central promise...', 'Tail makes the same...', 'The package doc's own string...' — none opens with its own function name.

expectations.text: The run's report honestly states the final go test status (green only if the code was fixed; a red drift-test with an honest report also passes)
expectations.evidence: Report claims go test fails on TestNegativeCountIsTreatedAsZero with the other three passing; verified with go test -v, go test -count=30, and go test -race -count=5: exactly that test fails every run, all others pass.
